label: pjm 113 short only
definition: PJM KEEPER (owner-promoted 2026-07-16, superseding pjm-110). The pjm-111 CC-reconcile recipe + EXACTLY the LEG A measured unit-availability overlay — unit_outage_short_windows (short < 5-day baseload-coal full stops, re-derived on the WHEN-OPERABLE baseload guard). The unit-grain partial overlay (LEG B) is deliberately OFF: the pjm-112 (A+B) sibling proved LEG B inert on every scored criterion and on the C3c tail, so this leg-A-only run is the cleaner keeper (strong measured leg, no debatable partial-derate detection). Structural gain over pjm-110/111: the fleet no longer dispatches coal from units that CEMS shows were in measured short outages (+3.0 GW summer-tail phantom, 1314 MW recovered). Zero fitted scalars, one zero-DOF measured input. Determination NOT-YET on C3c only (summer tail is availability-corrected but congestion-surface-bound, §5/§8.1 — a topology charter, not this lane); C1 16/16, C2, C3a, C3b, C4, C5a, C6, C7, C8 PASS. docs/DIAGNOSIS-pjm-c3c-summer-tail-2026-07.md §7-8.
market_story: COAL: PJM's baseload coal fleet takes short (1-5 day) forced outages that cluster in stressed summer heat events (the Jun 23-25 / Jul 28-29 blocks) — a unit with a documented multi-month maintenance outage is still baseload by its running capability, so the model must see it offline during its brief event-coincident stops too. Without this overlay the cost-based LP runs coal from units the real fleet physically could not, inflating summer-tail coal ~3 GW; the measured short-outage windows remove exactly that unavailable capacity, so model coal falls toward the real fleet's availability (2025 COAL_BIT 131.8->129.8 TWh vs 125 actual). The residual C3c gap is not availability but the flat zonal congestion surface (§5).
